questions.q: Which of these is an INPUT device?
Which part of the computer carries out instructions and does the processing?
Which type of memory loses its contents when the computer is switched off?
A touch screen is an example of...
options: both an input device and an output device

questions.q: Which of these is an example of system software?
Which job is done by the operating system?
options: Writing letters and reports for the user
Managing files and sharing the computer's memory and processor between programs

questions.q: A mouse is an output device.
questions.explain: A mouse sends data INTO the computer, so it is an input device.

questions.q: Software is the set of instructions (programs) that tells the hardware what to do.
RAM keeps its data permanently, even when the power is off.
questions.explain: RAM is volatile: its data is lost when the power is off.

questions.q: A printer can be used to produce a hard copy (a paper copy) of a document.
The ____ is the part of the computer that carries out instructions.
A monitor and a printer are examples of ____ devices.
Programs such as a word processor or spreadsheet are called ____ software.
The physical parts of a computer that you can touch are called ____.
State two examples of input devices.
questions.answer: Any two from: keyboard, mouse, microphone, scanner, webcam, touch screen, joystick.

questions.q: Explain the difference between hardware and software.
questions.answer: Hardware is the physical parts of a computer that you can touch (1). Software is the programs / instructions that run on the hardware (1).

questions.q: Give two reasons why a computer needs an operating system.
questions.answer: Any two from: manages hardware and memory; lets the user interact with the computer (user interface); runs and manages applications; manages files and folders; provides security (passwords/accounts).

questions.q: Match each device to what it is used for.
pairs: Storing files you can carry with you

questions.q: Match each software example to its type.
Match each term to its meaning.
pairs: Temporary memory for programs in use
